prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the downward-sloping ground plane of the paved road and right-side dirt shoulder stretching from roughly 1.2 m below the camera wearer to over 5 m ahead, with no other people present in the scene. In frames 1 and 2, the camera wearer's own legs (around 1.2–1.5 m away at the bottom center-left) and outstretched hands (within arm's reach at 0.5–0.8 m at the bottom left and right) appear brighter than the road surface, while a partial vehicle wheel on the upper left of frame 2 (about 1.8 m away) and a round leaf bowl to its right (about 2.2 m away and 0.8 m from the wheel) stand out against the darker background. Across frames 2 to 4, the camera wearer approaches and bends toward the bowl as it shifts from the upper center to the lower-left foreground and brightens markedly to within arm's reach (about 0.4–0.6 m away) while being held by the wearer's hand at the bottom edge, before the view tilts up in frame 5 to show the receding road up to 8–10 m ahead. The map clearly separates the 3D relief of the raised tire, the concave bowl rim, and the wearer's limbs from the flat asphalt—which is harder to gauge in RGB alone—and shows the limbs, tire, and held bowl partly clipped by the lower and left frame boundaries. However, the monocular depth scale is inconsistent across frames, rendering the bowl in frame 3 as a floating mid-grey disc darker than the surrounding ground at the same distance and over-brightening the right-hand road edge in frame 5 as if it were an obstacle less than 0.5 m away.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map leaves the paved road, dirt shoulder, and frame 2 vehicle wheel unlabelled in black, isolating only fragments of the camera wearer's body at the bottom of frames 1–2 and the leaf bowl in frame 3–4, while confirming no other people are present or facing the camera wearer. In frames 1 and 2, the wearer's left hand, lower legs/feet (1.2–1.5 m below), and right hand (within arm's reach at 0.5–0.8 m on the bottom right) are split into separatecoloured masks labelled 'person' that are partially cut off by the bottom frame edge and separated by about 0.3–0.5 m laterally. As the camera wearer walks forward and reaches down in frame 4, the leaf bowl—now held within arm's reach at 0.4–0.6 m in the lower-left foreground—is segmented as a large tan mask, whereas in frames 2, 3, and 5 the bowl on the ground (1.3–2.2 m ahead) and the wearer's fingertips at the bottom edge are completely missed. This map provides crisp pixel boundaries between the wearer's limbs and the ground in frames 1–2 and outlines the held bowl in frame 4 where the wearer's fingers slightly occlude its bottom rim. However, it is highly unreliable in both semantics and recall: it splits a single ego-body into multiple 'person' instances, misclassifies the close-up leaf bowl as a 'sandwich', hallucinates a purple 'surfboard' mask on a patch of dirt/concrete at the top-right edge of frame 3 (about 2 m away), and fails to detect any objects in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only magenta hand skeletons against a black background with no yellow body skeletons, reflecting that no other people are in the scene and that the camera wearer's head and torso are behind the egocentric viewpoint facing forward and downward along the road. In frames 1 and 2, a single magenta hand skeleton tracks the camera wearer's right hand in the lower-right foreground within arm's reach (roughly 0.5–0.7 m in front of and below the camera, about 0.3 m to the right of the wearer's legs), with the palm angled inward and fingers curled slightly toward the ground. Across frames 1 to 2, this right hand shifts slightly downward and to the right as the wearer steps forward toward the tire (1.8 m away on the left) and the leaf bowl (2.2 m away on the right), before disappearing below the frame in frame 3 as the wearer approaches the bowl. The map makes the fine 3D finger articulation and joint orientation of the wearer's right hand much clearer than the motion-blurred RGB frames alone. However, it is unreliable for full-scene body tracking because it misses the wearer's partially visible left hand at the bottom-left of frame 1, fails to detect the visible legs and feet in frames 1–3, and misses the right hand gripping the lower rim of the bowl at the bottom edge of frame 4.
